sections.passageText:
Australia was a country I always wanted to visit. This year I saved up some money and booked a flight to go travelling. I had some friends studying there, so it was a perfect opportunity to see friends and travel around.

The flight made me realize exactly how far away Australia is from home. I spent 10 hours flying from London to Hong Kong, then a further 8 hours to Sydney, my first stop in Australia. The flight went quite quickly though, since there were lots of films to keep me entertained.

When I arrived, I felt strange. Everything was upside down over there. It was the start of winter in May! Fortunately, for me the weather was still warm and sunny. It also took me a while to get used to the time difference.

Australia is truly beautiful. It is full of views and wildlife you would not find anywhere else in the world. One of the highlights of my trip was visiting a koala (考拉) reserve in Brisbane. There were koalas everywhere sleeping in the trees. I even got a chance to hold one. I learnt lots of facts about koalas too. They can sleep for up to 22 hours a day to save energy!

At the reserve there was also a big lawn full of kangaroos (袋鼠). We were allowed to feed and touch them. They were really cute and friendly. I loved visiting Australia, from the mountains and waterfalls in the National Parks to the long white sandy beaches. It's an incredible country and worth visiting. I'm already dreaming of going back!

questions.answerExplanation: 根据文章第一段第一句"Australia was a country I always wanted to visit."可知，作者一直渴望访问澳大利亚，该句提供的是正确信息。

questions.answerExplanation: 文章第一段提到"I had some friends studying there"，说明作者在澳大利亚有朋友，但没有提到在访问期间结交了新朋友，文中没有提及相关信息。

sections.passageText:
Veganism. What does it mean? To some of you, it might be a completely new word. And it's certainly a word I have only become familiar with in recent years. A vegan diet is one that contains no animal products. That means no meat, no milk, no eggs, etc.

I became interested in it on the internet. I came across a woman called Freelee. She claimed to regularly eat around fifty bananas a day to stay healthy.

Fifty bananas! I quickly realized that this was not the diet for me. However, what she was saying about veganism did "pique" my interest. And I went on to watch many more vegan videos. Eventually, I switched to veganism about six months ago.

I start off with a fruit drink made of bananas, berries and orange juice. For lunch, I typically have potato fries with a sweet sauce. For dinner I normally have rice with a tomato sauce and some vegetables. I even make tasty vegan puddings. One of my favorites is coconut cream mixed with chocolate powder and sugar.

While veganism is often associated with physical weakness, that is certainly not the case for me. I have discovered many delicious vegan products, which one might never consider as vegan. Personally, eating this way has given me a much more positive feeling

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, a vegan diet is ____.
questions.answerExplanation: 根据文章第一段最后一句"A vegan diet is one that contains no animal products. That means no meat, no milk, no eggs, etc."可知，纯素饮食不含动物产品。

questions.answerExplanation: 根据文章第二段"I became interested in it on the internet. I came across a woman called Freelee."以及后文提到watch vegan videos可知，作者是通过网络视频了解到纯素生活方式的。
"pique"在这里的意思是"引起、激发"，与"arouse"同义。"pique my interest"意为"引起我的兴趣"。

questions.answerExplanation: 根据文章第四段"While veganism is often associated with physical weakness, that is certainly not the case for me."以及第五段"Personally, eating this way has given me a much more positive outlook on life."（官方解析引用的措辞与试题卷印刷原文"...a much more positive feeling"略有出入，但结论一致）可知，作者认为她的纯素饮食是健康的。

options: A. attracted a lot of fans
B. had a positive attitude toward life
C. went on a special fruit-based diet
D. quickly recovered from a spider bite
questions.answerExplanation: 官方答案为D，解析引用"Kristina was bitten by a deadly spider... Yet she made a full and speedy recovery."，但试题卷实际印刷的短文（见本节passageText，共5段）全文并未出现"Kristina"或"spider"相关内容。该题缺乏原文依据，需人工核对原始试卷图像确认短文是否完整（详见parsingNotes）。

①Over the last 15 years, more and more people in the US have been drinking bottled water. There is no sign of slowing down. In fact, sales of bottled water are going up faster than any other kind of drink. It is true even in cities where it is safe to drink tap water. This has been a disaster for the environment and for our health.

②Most bottled water comes from underground water. Much of this underground water could have flowed into rivers and lakes. Using this water can make droughts (干旱) more serious. Many companies use water from mountain glaciers (冰川), but this is not much better. When the glacier melts, the water usually flows to areas like rivers or wetlands. When companies take glacier water, they take it from areas that need it.

③It takes about 1.6 liters of water to make one liter of bottled water. This wastes a lot of water. Also transporting the bottled water to stores burns fuel and creates pollution. The problems do not stop when the water reaches people who buy it. Water bottles are made from plastic which does not break down. Although it can be recycled, people usually do not put it in the recycle can.

④Some may say that bottled water is safer and healthier than tap water. But that is not true. Sometimes chemicals or bacteria get into bottled water, and companies have to destroy them. Actually, tap water is often healthier than bottled water. Bottled water may lack fluoride (氟化物) which helps protect our teeth. Fluoride is found in tiny amounts in tap water.

⑤Obviously, more people need to know that tap water is safer and healthier. Unfortunately, tap water cannot advertise itself. When a product that is cheaper and better does not win, that is bad news. When the product is water, we all lose.

options: B. Harmful elements in bottled water

sections.passageText:
Every year hundreds of species of birds take long trips. ___(26)___ In the fall, they fly to warmer climates where food is plentiful all winter. When spring comes, they fly back to raise their young where they were born. For a long time people wondered where the birds went and what routes they took.

Researchers now know that migrating birds are guided by their own sorts of maps and compasses. But it has taken many decades to uncover the secrets of these navigation (导航) tools. In the 1800s, scientists started putting bands around birds' legs. ___(27)___ When people found the banded birds, they contacted the person named on the band and told him where and when they had found the bird. In this simple way, scientists learned a lot about where birds traveled, where they stopped, and how fast they moved.

Today scientists still put bands on birds' legs. They also use new ways of tracking birds such as airplanes, computers, and satellites. ___(28)___

Birds often migrate in groups. You may have seen Canada geese flying high in the sky in a V-form. Young birds follow their parents. ___(29)___ They may follow a river and remember what it looks like. Also, birds use the position of the sun and stars as a compass to find their way.

___(30)___ Chemicals in their brains allow them to sense the magnetic field and travel in the right direction. But scientists are still researching how this happens. They think some birds may actually be able to see the earth's magnetic field.

options: A. The bands contained a name and address.
B. Birds use the earth's magnetic field to navigate too.
C. A map and a compass are often helpful for long trips.
D. They fly thousands of miles from one home to another.
E. They learn the route that the older geese have traveled before.
F. They have answered many questions about how birds navigate.

sections.passageTitle: My Hometown and My College Town
sections.passageText: My hometown and my college town have several things in common. First, both are ___(31)___ communities. My hometown, Gridlock, has a population of only about 10,000 people. Similarly, my college town, Subnormal, ___(32)___ of about 11,000 local residents. This population rises to 15,000 people when the college students are ___(33)___ classes. Second, both are located in rural areas. Gridlock is surrounded by farmland, which is devoted ___(34)___ to growing corn and beans. Likewise, Subnormal lies in the ___(35)___ of farmland that is used to ___(36)___ pigs and cattle. Third, both contain college campuses. Gridlock is ___(37)___ to Neutron College, which is famous for its Agricultural Economics program. In the same ___(38)___, Subnormal boasts the ___(39)___ campus of Quark College, which is well ___(40)___ for its Agricultural Engineering Department.

questions.answerExplanation: 根据后文"has a population of only about 10,000 people"可知，这两个都是小社区，所以选small。

questions.stem: 第32空：Subnormal ___ of about 11,000 local residents
questions.answerExplanation: consist of 是固定搭配，意为"由...组成"，这里是说大学城由大约11000名当地居民组成。

questions.answerExplanation: attend classes 是固定搭配，意为"上课"，这里是说当大学生上课时，人口增加到15000人。

questions.answerExplanation: mainly 意为"主要地"，这里是说Gridlock被农田包围，主要种植玉米和豆类。

questions.answerExplanation: in the center of 是固定搭配，意为"在...中心"，这里是说Subnormal位于养猪养牛的农田中心。

questions.answerExplanation: raise pigs and cattle 意为"养猪和牛"，raise 在这里是"饲养"的意思。

questions.answerExplanation: be home to 是固定搭配，意为"是...的所在地"，这里是说Gridlock是Neutron College的所在地。
in the same way 是固定搭配，意为"同样地"，这里是说同样地，Subnormal也有Quark College美丽的校园。试题卷词库选项印刷为"L.Way"（首字母大写），句中实际应为小写"way"，为印刷格式问题，不影响答案字母L。

questions.answerExplanation: beautiful campus 意为"美丽的校园"，这里是说Subnormal拥有Quark College美丽的校园。

questions.answerExplanation: be well known for 是固定搭配，意为"以...闻名"，这里是说该学院以其农业工程系而闻名。

sections.passageText: Technology has become an essential part of our daily life. It ___(41)___ (accompany) us everywhere we go. Digital technology, in the form of smart ___(42)___ (phone), web-based TVs and computers, is ___(43)___ (change) the world, especially for advertisers. Consumers today interact with ads in new ways. They can ___(44)___ (easy) take part in surveys or just turn them off if they want to. They can also promote a brand by ___(45)___ (suggest) how good a product is to other people. Social media networks also play an ___(46)___ (importance) part in global advertising strategies. People also want relevant ads on their screens. While they browse the Internet, it would be ___(47)___ (help) for such ads to show up. Internet ___(48)___ (user) click on these ads more often if they look for relevant ___(49)___ (inform). Advertisers are now ___(50)___ (face) with a great challenge: using new technology to form new relationships with customers and create new business models.

questions.answerExplanation: 主语是It，第三人称单数，一般现在时，所以用accompanies。
smart phone是可数名词，这里用复数形式phones表示一类事物。
前面有is，这里用现在进行时，所以用changing。
这里需要副词修饰动词短语take part in，所以用easily。
by是介词，后面接动名词形式，所以用suggesting。
这里需要形容词修饰名词part，所以用importance的形容词形式important。
这里需要形容词作表语，所以用help的形容词形式helpful。
user是可数名词，这里用复数形式users表示一类人。
relevant后面接名词，inform的名词形式是information，意为"信息"。
be faced with 是固定搭配，意为"面临"，所以用faced。

questions.stem: 请根据所提供材料中的要求完成一篇100词左右的英文写作任务（题为"Safe Journey"）。要点：①旅途中安全的重要性；②旅途中应该特别注意的事项。
questions.answerExplanation:
官方参考范文：

Safe Journey

Traveling is one of the most exciting experiences in life, but safety should always come first. A safe journey not only ensures our physical well-being but also allows us to fully enjoy the beauty of the trip.

During the journey, we should pay special attention to several important matters. First, we should always keep our personal belongings safe, especially valuable items like wallets, passports and electronic devices. It's better to carry them in a secure bag that stays close to our body. Second, we should be aware of our surroundings at all times, especially in crowded places or unfamiliar areas. Avoid walking alone at night in unknown neighborhoods. Third, we should follow traffic rules strictly, whether we are driving or walking as pedestrians. Fourth, we should keep in touch with family or friends, letting them know our whereabouts regularly.

In conclusion, safety is the foundation of a pleasant journey. By taking these simple precautions, we can ensure that our travels are not only enjoyable but also safe.

（此为官方参考范文，非唯一标准答案，官方未提供额外的分项评分细则。）
